the development of cholinergic function in the human fetal brain.

the fetal cortex has a high ChAT activity, but that it is not accompanied by the expected cholinergic receptors, suggesting that the fetal cortex is not yet cholinergic.

in the human fetal cortex cholinergic function, as reflected by ChAT activity, receptor binding, AChE activity, and histochemistry, develops during the second trimesters and that the development is not completed by the end of the fetal period.
cholinergic receptor activity in the developing human cortex, although detectable at 14 weeks, is relatively low and may not be fully expressed before the third trimester.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human brain is a cholinergic system in the early stage of development.
in human fetal brain, cortical cholinesterase activity and choline acetylase activity are comparable with that of the adult brain.
the cholinergic system in the human fetal neocortex is present and functionally active at a time when the cortex is undergoing a period of rapid neurogenesis and synaptogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cholinergic receptor expression in the cortex is not established until late in gestation and that the development of cholinergic function in the human fetal cortex may be a relatively late event.
there is no evidence for a critical period in the human brain for cholinergic receptor expression.
the human fetus, at least in the second trimester, is not only able to metabolize cholinergic neurotransmitters, but also has the capacity to bind cholinergic receptors.
